newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi Heavy, US firm to design Malaysia LNG plant.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi Heavy, US firm to design Malaysia LNG plant.

text.p: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd said on Friday that it has been awarded a contract to draft the basic design for a liquefied natural gas (LNG) plant in Malaysia together with U.S. group Fluor Daniels.
The design is for a plant with a production capacity of 6.8 million tonnes. The plant will be built by Malaysia LNG Tiga Sdn Bhd, a Mitsubishi Heavy spokesman said.
The plant is expected to be the world's largest LNG production facility once it is completed.
The contract calls for the two firms to draft the design and prepare documents related to the project.
Media reports have said that the contract awarded was worth about $10 million, with an additional $50-60 million paid if the companies also undertook project management.
The spokesman declined to comment on the specific sum, but said that news reports were "not far off the target".

Under conditions for the project, the company that has been awarded the contract to draft the design cannot take part in a tender, due to take place next year, for the actual construction of the plant, the spokesman said.
The plant is scheduled to be completed in 2001.
This is the first time that Mitsubishi has won a contract related to an LNG plant project, the spokesman said.
Malaysia LNG Tiga is a joint venture between Petronas, the state government of eastern Sarawak state, Nippon Oil Co Ltd, Occidental LNG (Malaysia) Ltd and Shell Gas BV.
